# What Size Power Station Do You Need to Run a Fridge?

**Short answer:** For a typical full-size fridge, get a station with **at least 1,200–1,500W of surge** and **about 1,000Wh to cover most of a day, or 1,400–2,000Wh to cover a full 24 hours.** It must also have **pure sine wave** output.

## The three checks

**1. Running watts (easy).** A full-size fridge draws about 100–250W while the compressor runs. Almost any 1,000W-class station handles this. ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage))

**2. Startup surge (this is where most stations fail).** When the compressor kicks on, it briefly spikes to about **1,000–2,400W**, depending on the fridge:

| Fridge type | Running | Startup surge to clear |
|---|---|---|
| Mini/compact | 50–100W | 300–600W |
| Top-freezer (18–21 cu ft) | 100–200W | 1,000–1,800W |
| French-door / side-by-side | 150–250W | 1,500–2,400W |
| Older/inefficient | 200–350W | 1,800–2,400W+ |

([BlackBox](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))

If the surge rating is too low, the station shuts off the moment the fridge tries to start, no matter how big the battery is.

**3. Battery capacity (Wh) sets how long it runs.** The compressor only runs about 30–40% of the time, so a typical fridge averages roughly **40–70W** over a day ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).

## Calculate it for your own fridge

1. Find the kWh/year figure on your fridge's yellow EnergyGuide label, or look up your model in the DOE's refrigerator rating search tool ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-size-a-portable-power-station-for-a-refrigerator-and-essential-devices/)).
2. Divide kWh/year by 8.76 to get average watts. For example, 362 kWh/yr ÷ 8.76 ≈ 41W.
3. Multiply average watts by the hours of outage, then divide by 0.85 for inverter losses. Add about 20% headroom.
   - Example: 41W × 24h ÷ 0.85 × 1.2 ≈ **1,400Wh for one day** ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator))

Large side-by-sides with ice makers can use twice that. Hot kitchens and frequent door opening also push usage up.

## Picks by outage length

**About 1,000Wh: most of a day (around 16–17 hours)**
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**: 1,070Wh, ~$499 ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))
- **Anker SOLIX C1000**: 1,056Wh, ~$470 ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))
- **Bluetti AC180**: 1,152Wh, 1,800W continuous / 2,700W peak ([BlackBox](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage))

**About 1,500Wh: a full day for a typical fridge**
- **Anker SOLIX F1500**: 1,536Wh, 1,800W / 2,400W surge, $599.99 (down from $1,199.99) when checked Oct 22 ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator))

**About 2,000Wh: roughly 33 hours, or a fridge plus a few essentials**
- **Bluetti AC200L**: 2,048Wh, 2,400W continuous, expandable to 8kWh. It's $899, or **$854.05 with code AFF5OFF** (5% off, reported working in Bluetti's cart on Oct 21). Note that this is an affiliate link: [Buy at Bluetti](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l) ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l))
- **Anker SOLIX S2000**: 2,010Wh, 1,500W / 3,000W peak, $699.99 after coupon ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator))
- **EcoFlow Delta 3 Max** (2,048Wh, ~$879) or **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** (2,042Wh, ~$899) ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))

**Tip:** Test your fridge on the station before an outage. During an outage, keep the door shut, which noticeably stretches runtime.

If you tell me your fridge's kWh/year figure and how long your outages usually last, I can narrow this down to one pick.
